decisive_items: the right lower lip deviates inward, whereas the rest of facial movement is symmetric
frowning, forehead wrinkling, eye closure, and nasolabial fold depth are symmetric on both sides
Magnetic resonance imaging of the temporal bones and internal auditory canals is normal
response.rationale: Isolated lower lip depression on smiling with all other facial movements symmetric and normal imaging points specifically to congenital unilateral lower lip palsy (depressor anguli oris hypoplasia), not generalized facial palsy or Moebius syndrome.

rejected.why: Too broad; does not capture the isolated lower lip involvement with otherwise symmetric facial function.
Moebius syndrome requires abducens palsy and often other cranial nerve deficits; here eye closure, forehead, and nasolabial folds are symmetric and imaging is normal.
Isolated congenital facial paresis is less specific; the vignette emphasizes isolated lower lip involvement, which is the hallmark of congenital unilateral lower lip palsy.
